szoveg_eredeti:
A day after returning as chief executive at Nvidia, Jensen Huang apologized on Tuesday to his entire company for violating its code of conduct during an hourlong meeting that began somber before transforming into a defiant airing of grievances.

“I made some terrible mistakes,” he said. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”

Mr. Huang said he is in therapy and that he had written some of the company’s code of conduct. It was “not acceptable,” he said, that he violated the code of conduct. He said that his actions had forced the company’s board of directors to evaluate his future with the company, which led him to resign on Nov. 11.

But Mr. Huang also sought to dismiss two narratives about his return. He said he wasn’t back because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” and “above the code of conduct.” Nor was he back, he said, because President Trump pressured Nvidia’s board of directors to reinstate him.

“That is completely untrue,” Mr. Huang said in a livestream that was reviewed by The New York Times. He said he was back because Nvidia’s board “evaluated the entire situation” and “gathered facts.” They also received assurances from the Trump administration that Mr. Huang was not a national security threat and deserved a second chance.

Mr. Huang disagreed with reports that he was an abusive boss. He attacked criticism of the company’s structure, in which he has 60 direct reports. And he boasted that he doesn’t “believe in succession planning” because it would imply some executives were more important than others.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

Tripp Mickle reports for The Times on some of the world’s biggest tech companies, including Nvidia, Google and Apple. He also writes about tech industry trends like layoffs and artificial intelligence.

Kalley Huang is a Times reporter in San Francisco, covering the technology industry and its largest companies, including Nvidia and Apple.
